title: Industrial Policy Delivers A Fiscal Payoff
text:
Industrial Policy Delivers A Fiscal Payoff

Tilly Zhang

Gavekal Dragonomics | 25 Sep 2026

This year’s string of blockbuster IPOs in China has created enormous paper wealth for some local governments, which are significant shareholders in the latest generation of technology companies. Government entities have dominated venture-capital investing in China for years (see Venture Capital Rebounds), but more companies are now going public, allowing more investments to pay off. Local authorities have long used equity investments as a tool of industrial policy and economic development; with financial gains becoming more common, the finances of successful governments are also being transformed.The Beijing, Shenzhen and Shanghai governments all invested in Unitree Robotics, and after its August IPO their stakes are worth about RMB14bn. Display maker HKC, which went public in June, has multiple local-government backers from Chongqing, Sichuan, Guizhou, Hunan and Anhui; their combined stakes are worth about RMB37bn.
